common_thread.question: What keeps returning across your heroes?
common_thread.question_body: Pick the kind of help that feels most like your default.
common_thread.correct_feedback: Yes — {trait} is the strongest recurring way of helping across your established pool.
common_thread.incorrect_feedback: {selected} shows up in the pool, but {trait} keeps returning across more of your heroes.
common_thread.reveal: {trait} keeps returning across {hero_count} of your established heroes.
common_thread.boundary: This is the job your heroes keep offering, not a scorecard for every match.

no_clear_insight.headline: Your pool doesn't have one defining job.
no_clear_insight.body: Your established heroes keep solving different problems. That range is the point.

exception.question: Which hero gives your pool a different kind of Dota?
exception.question_body: Pick the hero you expect to feel most different from the rest.
exception.incorrect: Good guess — but not this one.
exception.correct_feedback: Yes — {hero} stands apart from the rest of the pool most clearly.
exception.incorrect_feedback: {selected} fits the pool more closely. {hero} stands apart more clearly.
exception.no_clear_feedback: {selected} is a plausible read, but no single hero stands apart clearly enough.

no_clear_insight.headline: Your pool has no odd one out.
no_clear_insight.body: Several heroes cover similar ground, so no single pick stands apart clearly enough to earn the odd-one-out label.
no_clear_insight.boundary: Different does not mean better or worse.

exception.answer: {hero} is the clearest outlier in this pool.
exception.reveal: {hero} stands apart from the rest of the pool more clearly than the alternatives.
exception.boundary: Different does not mean better or worse.

evolution.question: How do you think your hero pool has changed recently?
evolution.question_body: Choose the description that feels closest. This is your read before the reveal.
evolution.unavailable: Your pool has not changed shape clearly enough to show it yet.
evolution.unavailable_heading: Pool Evolution is taking a rain check.
evolution.locked: Complete the self-assessment above to see the reveal.
evolution.option_same_style: My heroes changed, but my style didn’t
evolution.option_different_kind: I’ve shifted toward a different kind of hero

new_heroes_new_toolkit.heading: Your pool changed direction.
new_heroes_new_toolkit.body: The names are not the only thing changing. The kind of Dota available in your pool is changing too.

new_heroes_same_toolkit.heading: New heroes. Same taste.
new_heroes_same_toolkit.body: Your recent picks look different, but the jobs you keep asking them to perform barely moved.

stable_core_new_branch.heading: Your pool is growing a new branch.
stable_core_new_branch.body: Your familiar core is still intact, but a different kind of hero is beginning to appear more often.

broadly_stable.heading: More stable than it feels.
broadly_stable.body: The edges moved a little, but your core hero mix and its favourite jobs stayed recognizable.

hero_mirror.title: Your Hero Mirror
hero_mirror.closed: One last comparison: the hero whose games look most like your usual Dota.
hero_mirror.available: Among the heroes you return to, {hero} looks most like your usual Dota.
hero_mirror.unavailable: No played hero looks enough like your usual Dota to earn the mirror yet.
hero_mirror.qualifier: Not your best hero. Not necessarily your most played.
hero_mirror.guardrail: This is not a personality test. You are not {hero}; your games on {hero} simply rhyme most with the way you usually play.

element.observation: Across these matches, {label} landed in the {zone} zone.
element.distinctive: This is one of the clearest pieces of your game.
element.evidence: The pattern has a shape you can recognize in your games.
element.notice: The zone is a clue, not a verdict.
element.guardrail: This describes an observed pattern, not why it happened.

pattern.worth_noticing: The surrounding Elements give this pattern its shape.
pattern.player_read: This is how the signals moved together; it is not a claim about a cause.
pattern.takeaway: Keep an eye on whether the same relationship appears in another window.
pattern.guardrail: This is a useful pattern, not a verdict about you.

pattern_action.same_playbook_heading: Where do you want to take this?
pattern_action.same_playbook_intro: Both directions are valid: keep your familiar answer, or add range without abandoning your anchors.
pattern_action.same_playbook_deepen_description: More heroes that keep your current game familiar.
pattern_action.same_playbook_stretch_description: Bridge heroes that add a new answer while preserving an anchor.
pattern_action.same_playbook_empty_direction: The direction is useful, but the next hero is still keeping a low profile.
pattern_action.comfort_edge_kicker: Build the pool with a reason
pattern_action.comfort_edge_heading: Your strongest heroes are the safest part of this pool today.
pattern_action.comfort_edge_intro: The other established heroes can still be worth learning. This is your ladder, not the meta's.
pattern_action.partial_transfer_heading: One learning demand may explain the gap
pattern_action.partial_transfer_unresolved_heading: The gap is real; the reason is still hiding

pattern_action.presence_tax_unresolved_body: The cost has a shape, but the context is still slippery.

P01_BROAD_HERO_NARROW_JOB.headline: Broad by hero. Narrow by job.
P01_BROAD_HERO_NARROW_JOB.subheadline: Your hero names change more than the ways you tend to help underneath.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: Your pool offers variety on the surface, but several heroes keep asking you to solve a similar kind of Dota problem.

fallback.title: The pattern is clear; the next hero is not
fallback.body: The repeated job is clear. The next hero can wait until a useful bridge appears.

P01_ADD_MISSING_FUNCTION.title: Add one missing answer
P01_ADD_MISSING_FUNCTION.body: Try {hero_name} when you want to keep a familiar anchor while adding a genuinely different way to help.

P01_DRAFT_SPECIFIC_EXPANSION.title: Deep Dive: expand the answer
P01_DRAFT_SPECIFIC_EXPANSION.body: Replay and draft detail could show which matchups make a new answer valuable.

P02_RELIABILITY_LADDER.headline: Your pool has a reliability ladder.
P02_RELIABILITY_LADDER.subheadline: Some established heroes are anchors; others are still becoming dependable.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: The development side is not a verdict. It is the clearest practice order inside the heroes you already return to.

fallback.title: The ladder is still forming
fallback.body: Your pool is broad, but the rungs are not far enough apart to call out a neat order yet.

P02_FOCUS_DEVELOPMENT_ORDER.title: Practice #3–5 with a reason
P02_FOCUS_DEVELOPMENT_ORDER.body: Work down the development side one hero at a time, and name the new demand each hero introduces.

P02_HERO_DEMAND_COMPARISON.title: Deep Dive: hero demand
P02_HERO_DEMAND_COMPARISON.body: Match-level detail could separate hero familiarity from the specific demands that change your results.

P03_PRESENCE_HOLDS_RESULT_BENDS.headline: Your presence travels farther than your results.
P03_PRESENCE_HOLDS_RESULT_BENDS.subheadline: You still show up in fights on off-pool heroes. The results stop travelling with you.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: The match history shows a result difference and one useful learning lead. It does not say the lead caused the gap.

fallback.title: The transfer split is visible
fallback.body: Your familiar and off-pool games separate, but the reason is still hiding.

P03_PRACTICE_TRANSFER_DEMAND.title: Practice the demand, not the label
P03_PRACTICE_TRANSFER_DEMAND.body: Use the strongest supported demand as a practice question, while treating the result difference as an observation rather than a cause.

P03_ENTRY_HOLD_REENTRY.title: Deep Dive: where transfer bends
P03_ENTRY_HOLD_REENTRY.body: Replay detail could separate entry, hold, and re-entry so the lead becomes easier to test.

P04_COMPACT_POOL_BROAD_JOBS.headline: Small pool. Different answers.
P04_COMPACT_POOL_BROAD_JOBS.subheadline: Your core stays compact while its ways to help reach across several jobs.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: The family map shows where the core overlaps and where only one or two heroes carry a job. It is a read on your options, not a claim about execution.

fallback.title: No versatile-core headline yet
fallback.body: Your compact pool has different answers, but none stands out enough to lead the chapter yet.

P04_ADD_MISSING_FUNCTION.title: Add a genuinely new tool
P04_ADD_MISSING_FUNCTION.body: Try {hero_name} only if it adds a missing way to help while keeping one familiar anchor.

P04_DRAFT_SPECIFIC_EXPANSION.title: Deep Dive: draft-specific options
P04_DRAFT_SPECIFIC_EXPANSION.body: Draft and matchup detail could test whether a missing function is useful in the situations you actually face.

P05_PROVEN_FLEX_WINDOW.headline: Your flexibility shows up in the window.
P05_PROVEN_FLEX_WINDOW.subheadline: The roster changed, and the range of ways to help kept returning together.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: This is more than a list of one-off picks: multiple heroes and jobs kept recurring in the same stretch.

fallback.title: Range is present, but distributed
fallback.body: The history shows a wide pool without one clean flex window that holds together across every comparison.

P05_PROTECT_RELIABLE_ANCHORS.title: Keep the anchors warm
P05_PROTECT_RELIABLE_ANCHORS.body: Protect the heroes that make this flexibility repeatable instead of trying to keep the whole roster equally ready.

P05_CONTEXT_TRANSFER.title: Deep Dive: context transfer
P05_CONTEXT_TRANSFER.body: Match-level detail could show which team, draft, and timing contexts support the flexible window.

P06_POST_LOSS_STRONGER.headline: LOSS → NEXT GAME: STRONGER
P06_POST_LOSS_STRONGER.subheadline: A familiar hero or job context is the strongest supported rebound setting.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: Your next game tends to improve after a loss. The pattern says nothing about your mood or motive.

fallback.title: The next game is stronger overall
fallback.body: The rebound is supported at a broad level, but no narrower hero or job context is stable enough to call out.

P06_REPEAT_POST_LOSS_ANCHOR.title: Simplify the first decision
P06_REPEAT_POST_LOSS_ANCHOR.body: Use the most repeatable familiar job as a post-loss anchor when you want one controllable next step.

P06_POST_LOSS_MECHANISM.title: Deep Dive: the rebound transition
P06_POST_LOSS_MECHANISM.body: Match-level detail could show what changes between the loss and the stronger next game.

P07_POST_LOSS_WEAKER.headline: LOSS → NEXT GAME: WEAKER
P07_POST_LOSS_WEAKER.subheadline: A familiar hero or job context is the strongest supported drop setting.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: Your next game tends to lose ground after a loss. The pattern does not establish tilt, panic, or hero causality.

fallback.title: The next game is weaker overall
fallback.body: The slide is supported at a broad level, but no narrower context is stable enough to call out.

P07_CHANGE_ONE_TRANSITION.title: Change one transition
P07_CHANGE_ONE_TRANSITION.body: Pause the queue, return to a stable hero or job, or simplify the first game plan—choose one controllable change.

P07_POST_LOSS_MECHANISM.title: Deep Dive: the slide transition
P07_POST_LOSS_MECHANISM.body: Match-level detail could show where the next-game result diverges from the usual shape.

P08_HIGH_PRESENCE_LOW_COST.headline: You can be involved without paying the full cost.
P08_HIGH_PRESENCE_LOW_COST.subheadline: The cleanest context combines high presence with lower death exposure.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: Your games identify a context where involvement and survival move together. It does not prove positioning skill or the value of every death.

fallback.title: The broad relationship is clear
fallback.body: High presence and lower exposure coexist overall, but no narrower context is stable enough to call out.

P08_PRESERVE_LOW_COST_PRESENCE.title: Preserve the useful shape
P08_PRESERVE_LOW_COST_PRESENCE.body: Keep the behavior or hero demand that produces high involvement without the same death exposure.

P08_FIGHT_CONTEXTS.title: Deep Dive: fight contexts
P08_FIGHT_CONTEXTS.body: Replay detail could identify which fight situations preserve involvement without the same death cost.

P09_HIGH_PRESENCE_HIGH_COST.headline: Your presence comes with a visible tax.
P09_HIGH_PRESENCE_HIGH_COST.subheadline: High involvement and high death exposure appear together in the supported history.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: The cost may be job-shaped, hero-specific, or spread across contexts. Your games cannot say whether those deaths bought useful value.

fallback.title: The cost is visible; its shape is not
fallback.body: The broad relationship is there, but no smaller context owns it clearly yet.

P09_INVESTIGATE_PRESENCE_COST.title: Separate necessary cost from exposure
P09_INVESTIGATE_PRESENCE_COST.body: Treat the strongest context as a question for replay review, not as proof that involvement itself is the problem.

P09_DEATH_VALUE_CONTEXT.title: Deep Dive: what deaths buy
P09_DEATH_VALUE_CONTEXT.body: Replay detail could separate initiation, space, saves, objectives, and deaths that buy nothing visible.

P10_SESSION_FADE.headline: Your session has a fade point.
P10_SESSION_FADE.subheadline: Your results usually start slipping later in longer sessions.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: The first clear fade point is a checkpoint for a different decision, not a magical curfew or a claim about why the change happens.

fallback.title: The curve fades gradually
fallback.body: Later-session movement is visible, but no single breakpoint is stable enough to call out.

P10_CHECKPOINT_AT_BREAKPOINT.title: Use the breakpoint as a checkpoint
P10_CHECKPOINT_AT_BREAKPOINT.body: At the first supported fade point, check whether a pause, stable hero, or simpler plan is the useful next experiment.

P10_SESSION_BREAKPOINT.title: Deep Dive: around the breakpoint
P10_SESSION_BREAKPOINT.body: Match-level detail could show what changes around the first clear session breakpoint.

P11_SESSION_RISE.headline: You tend to warm into the session.
P11_SESSION_RISE.subheadline: Your results usually improve later in longer sessions.

interpretation.title: The shape of it
interpretation.body: Your history shows a repeatable lift point. It is a planning clue, not a claim about focus, emotion, or a required number of games.

fallback.title: The curve rises gradually
fallback.body: Later-session movement is visible, but no single lift point is stable enough to call out.

P11_FRONTLOAD_FAMILIARITY.title: Front-load familiarity
P11_FRONTLOAD_FAMILIARITY.body: Use a reliable anchor early and defer experimentation if your history usually warms up over a session.

P11_SESSION_BREAKPOINT.title: Deep Dive: around the lift
P11_SESSION_BREAKPOINT.body: Match-level detail could show what changes before and after the first clear session lift point.
